articleTitle: Survey on Deep Learning based Automated Systems for the Detection and Grading of Diabetic Retinopathy using Retinal Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy is a common cause of blindness in people diagnosed as diabetic and it is developed as a subsequent condition by diabetes mellitus. Retinal fundus image analysis is commonly used for the computer aided diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy and its grading. Different automated systems based on deep learning techniques are available for the detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy using fundus image analysis. This article summarizes and analyses the performance of different deep learning based diabetic retinopathy detection and grading methods. Different types of image processing techniques used by the deep learning based algorithms and performance indicators used in the classification process are also discussed. This article also listed the publicly available datasets for Diabetic retinopathy detection and discussed the challenges that further need to be addressed in this area.

articleTitle: Self-Tuning Backstepping and Sliding Mode Control for Robust Trajectory Tracking in Differential Drive Wheeled Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust trajectory tracking control of a differential drive-wheeled mobile robot (DDWMR) with a unicycle model. A Lyapunov-based kinematic backstepping controller is developed to determine the necessary angular and linear velocities for the robot to move along the reference trajectory, considering only the kinematics of the robot. The velocity command generated by the kinematic controller is then passed to a dynamic controller. A sliding mode controller (SMC) is employed as the dynamic controller, providing robustness against external disturbances and variations in parameters. An adaptive law is implemented to self-tune the controller gains, ensuring accurate tracking of the reference trajectory. The stability of the closed-loop system is analyzed using the Lyapunov stability theory. Simulation results compared with a proportional integral derivative (PID) based dynamic controller demonstrate the robust performance of the proposed controller for trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Topology Identification of Low Voltage Distribution Networks using Smart Meter Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In distribution networks, changes to the topology information can occur frequently due to various reasons, such as weather conditions, routine maintenance, network reconfiguration etc. This often leads to missing or incorrect information regarding the distribution network model. To address this challenge, a <tex>$l$</tex><inf>2</inf>-regularized regression or Ridge regression has proposed in this paper. This method is suitable for the correlated injections which is common in current active distribution networks due to penetration of DERs in the network. Further, the proposed method doesn't required voltage angle. Therefore, the smart meter measurements are sufficient to correctly identifying the topology. The effectiveness of the suggested method is evaluated using a real 6-bus system and IEEE 33-bus system, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method is capable to identify the topology despite the limited number of measurements.

articleTitle: Machine Vision Techniques for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) is a precancerous condition of the cervix that, if left untreated, can develop into cervical cancer. Preventing cervical cancer requires the early detection and management of CIN. Machine vision techniques have the potential to greatly enhance CIN-C diagnosis and treatment. These methods can be used to examine digital images of cervical cells and determine whether any aberrant cells are present based on characteristics like size, shape, colour, and texture. Additionally, patterns in cervical cytology samples that are suggestive of CIN can be recognized by machine learning algorithms. The accuracy and specificity of CIN-C diagnosis can also be increased by combining machine vision with other technologies like optical coherence tomography and spectroscopy. Additionally, the development of portable and low-cost cervical cancer screening systems can increase access to healthcare in resource-limited settings. This paper reviews the current state of the art in machine vision techniques for CIN-C detection, highlighting recent developments and future perspectives in this field.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Load-Shedding Method for Renewable Integrated Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The risk of a blackout or system failure is growing as power networks get more complicated and larger on a regular basis as a result of rising demand and the adoption of contemporary technologies. Frequency stability plays a vital role for the safe operation of a power system. A power system's potential to go dark increases if its frequency abruptly increases or decreases. Frequency stability can be preserved by using an adaptive load-shedding technique to combat generation loss. In some circumstances, typical load shedding strategies struggles to deliver an adequate frequency response. This paper proposes a new dynamic-adaptive load shedding method as a solution to this problem. The proposed technique realizes the necessary crisis scenario, frequency variation caused by load damping, and ranking of load buses based on both frequency and voltage stability parameters, as well as the utilization of energy storage units (ESU) i.e. Battery Energy Storage System. The proposed method is used in conjunction with the IEEE 39 bus test system to evaluate its performance. Simulation results show that 201 MW, 451 MW of load shedding are necessary for generation loss occurrences of 600 MW, 800 MW respectively to maintain post-incident system frequency higher than the threshold value of 49.1 Hz. The proposed methodology ensures minimal adaptive load shedding in order to maintain satisfactory operation of the power system maintaining stable frequency and voltage margins.

articleTitle: A K-Medoids-LSTM Based Technique for Electromechanical Modes Identification for Synchrophasor Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this proposed work an efficient K-Medoids-LSTM based technique that takes into account of the degraded Phasor measurement unit (PMU) data for the estimation of poorly damped modes for wide area monitoring in smart grid is presented. This technique is designed in such a way that the detrimental effect of data missing and outliers which are created due to congestion in communication network, malfunction of PMUs or Phasor data concentrators (PDCs), and malicious attacks on mode estimation are mitigated. Here, the detection and removal of outliers are treated by applying K-Medoid algorithm, thereby the Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) is exploited for missing data imputation. Finally, total-least square-estimation-of-signal-parameters via rotational invariance technique (TLS-ESPRIT) is applied for mode estimation. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach is validated by conducting statistical analysis study on synthetic signal through Monte Carlo simulation and compared with other recently developed techniques. This technique is also validated on Two area data and real probing data obtained from Western Electricity Co-ordinating Council (WECC).

articleTitle: Two Stage EV Charger based on Bridgeless PFC Converter for e-Rickshaw
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Electric rickshaw is gaining popularity over their traditional counterpart due to their fuel cost reduction and less maintenance due to electric motor. In this paper, a two-stage onboard charger for EVs making use of a front-end interleaved power factor correction(PFC) converter coupled with a back-end Inductor Inductor Capacitor(LLC) Resonant Converter is proposed. The PFC converter outputs a voltage level of 400V which is regulated using the LLC Converter to 65V. This is used to charge an e-rickshaw battery. The presented converter is capable of regulating a steady output over a wide range of supply voltage levels maintaining a unity power factor. The addition of discontinuous conduction mode operation of the bridge-less PFC converter reduces the complexity of the control circuit by reducing the number of sensors required thereby improving the reliability of the converter and reducing the sensor-associated cost. Battery charging for Level 1 chargers with ratings 1kW-3.5KW is satisfied using this charging solution. Simulation results are depicted to show the working of the charger. The results show near unity power factor and THD levels within permissible limits.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Extractive Summarization Using Sentence Ranking Algorithm and Text Ranking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: It is possible to create an accurate and succinct summary using a method called automatic text summarising. Before creating the necessary summary sentences, the machine learning algorithms may be trained to understand documents and recognise the portions that transmit crucial facts and information. Abstractive text summa- rization and Extractive text summarization are its two methods. An extractive text summarization refers to the process of removing significant text from a text document or source manuscript. Deep learning techniques are used to train an abstractive text summarizer, which then generates new phrases and keywords based on the content of the original text. The process of acquiring and assimilation of the knowledge from numerous sources takes time. Automatic text summary is used to speed up the process of finding and consuming pertinent information. An extractive text summarising technique chooses crucial phrases, sentences, and other parts of the original text and concatenates them into a compressed form. The extractive text summarization produces grammatically correct sentences. The project is to develop a model that demonstrates extractive text summarization using sentence ranking and text rank algorithm. It shows that the text rank algorithm does a remarkable performance to extractive text summarization. Using a sentence ranking algorithm, extractive summaries are created that rate sentences according to their weights. In order to create a high-quality summary of the input document and store the summary as audio, the input document's highly scored sentences are extracted. A non-supervised, extractive text summarising method is called TextRank. While calculating the value of words and phrases in a document, the TextRank algorithm looks at how they relate to one another. According on how important the words are in each phrase, it then assigns a score to each one. The summary is formed using the algorithm's choice of the most crucial phrases.

articleTitle: A Survey on Stock Market Prediction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The stock market is a meeting point for buyers and sellers to buy and sell stocks. Stock price depends on local and global events. It has a dynamic, non-stationary nature. Thus, it is exceedingly challenging to make accurate stock price predictions. If we can predict the stock prices accurately, it will be helpful for investors. Many researches are going on in this area. Machine learning and deep learning methodologies are used for stock prediction. In this paper, a survey of different stock prediction techniques is done. Additionally, an approach that can give more accurate predictions than the techniques examined is suggested.

articleTitle: Wide Speed Range Control of PMSM Based on MTPA and Flux-Weakening Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This work gives a brief analysis of vector control strategy for field weakening (FW) and maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) operation of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Features such as higher efficiency, smaller size, faster dynamic response and large torque-to-inertia ratio makes the application of PMSM suitable for the electric vehicle (EV). However, because of permanent magnet on rotor, i.e., constant flux, permanent magnet (PM) motors have small constant power speed range (CPSR). This drawback limits the application of PMSM in EV's where wide speed operation, above base speed, is required. The high-speed operation under constant power zone can be extended either by increasing the output voltage of drive or by using FW control methods. However, the dc bus limits the output voltage of a conventional drive. Initially, in the constant torque zone MTPA control is implemented. Then constant voltage constant power (CVCP) FW strategy is implemented in the constant power zone. The above-mentioned vector control strategies have been simulated on a PMSM drive in MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Broken Rotor Bar Fault in 3-Φ Squirrel-Cage Induction Motors: A Critical Observations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: A critical analysis on broken rotor bar fault in three-phase induction motor is presented in this manuscript. Core research is carried on model-based broken bars fault detection and diagnosis for induction motors. A wide variety of faulty induction motor models are available in the literature. Out of which the model induction motor models based reference frames are widely used in fault diagnosis. It is believed to be a novel contribution, as researchers haven't considered whether these faulty models behave similar behaviour in stationary, rotor, synchronous and arbitrary reference frames. As an extension, a newly modified broken rotor induction motor model is proposed in this manuscript. To validate proposed idea dynamic computations of models are carried on using MATLAB R2022a programming software. The novel idea is verified with extensive simulation studies with various induction motors. The results and observations are presented clearly in this manuscript.

articleTitle: Sign language recognition of Malayalam alphabets using transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Sign languages, like any other natural language, rely on a set of symbols or gestures to convey meaning. The recognition of these symbols is crucial for the development of technologies that aim to improve communication between deaf and hearing individuals. This paper aims to use transfer learning to interpret the Indian sign language alphabets in Malayalam. This work also focuses on creating a dataset for the unified finger spelling alphabets in Malayalam language. The proposed method uses the ResNet50 model to classify images of static sign language alphabets into the corresponding letters of the alphabet. The method was evaluated and achieved an accuracy of 97.62% for training and 92.35% for validation.

articleTitle: Collision Avoidance Algorithm for a Quadrotor UAV in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The effectiveness of a quadrotor's mission is significantly determined by its ability to fly safely in its environment. Because quadrotors are frequently used in densely populated low-altitude airspace, collision avoidance algorithms are very important. If the anticipated trajectory can produce the least amount of jerk impact while still adhering to motion limit requirements, flight performance can be enhanced. Using a novel quadrotor collision avoidance algorithm, this study gives a trajectory with minimal jerk. The suggested method enables the quadrotor to follow a minimum jerk trajectory; however, when it encounters an obstacle, the quadrotor deviates from this trajectory and returns to the intended minimum jerk trajectory as the obstacle moves out of the way. This serves as the mission planning module for the quadrotor, and an autopilot proportional derivative controller then tracks the trajectory. The results of the flight simulation tests indicate that the quadrotor can successfully avoid linear and nonlinear moving objects. These simulations are conducted in the MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backstepping Control of 2-DOF Helicopter System Under Parametric Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The work presented in this paper is based on the design of adaptive backstepping control for a class of systems under parametric uncertainty. It considers 2-Degrees-Of-Freedom (2-DOF) helicopter system which is Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) system with non-linearities, uncertainties and coupled dynamics. The uncertain parameters are estimated by using adaptive laws. The estimated parameters are used in the design of the control law. The resulting closed-loop system with the designed control law is robust with respect to the uncertain parameters of the system. The stability of the system is proved theoretically. Simulation and experimental results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Reverse Engineering Piping and Instrumentation Drawings: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Data visualization is an easy way to communicate knowledge ever since human evolution. There are many visualization techniques including different types of plots, graphs, charts, and many more. Despite its usefulness, there is one common problem with visualization. The static image that generates the visualization is separated from the raw data. When a research study requires raw data it's hard to reverse engineer and take the raw data back. There are very limited tools available to reverse engineer and extract raw data from the above-mentioned static image. However, it's challenging to analyze all the data visualization techniques at a single glance. So, this research is focused on data extraction and summarization from Piping and Instrumental Drawings(P&ID). The dataset contains symbols taken from 2432 instances of piping and instrumental drawings. The goal of this study is to improve the accuracy of the prebuilt Convolutional Nural Network(CNN) model with hyperparameter optimization techniques and create a web application where users can extract and summarize text and symbols data from any piping and instrumentation drawing. As future directions, the applicability of other visualization techniques is also discussed at the conclusion.

articleTitle: Cluster Synchronization Conditions for Coupled Network of a Class of Nonlinear Systems Using Partial Contraction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The work presented here addresses a general frame-work for cluster synchronization of coupled nonlinear dynamical systems using contraction strategy. Here, sufficient conditions for cluster synchronization in coupled dynamical networks are derived using contraction, where each cluster in a network may have different nonlinear systems. The derived conditions for cluster synchronization with linear coupling function are sufficient to accurately characterise the network synchronisation behaviour in many real world problems. The linear coupling functions between the nodes of different clusters are considered to be bidirectional for both within and across the cluster connections. For validation, a network of three clusters of nodes with Lorenz, Lu and Chen dynamical systems, respectively, are used to illustrate the proposed analytical approach. The approach establishes exponential synchronization of corresponding states of systems constituting overall network.

articleTitle: A 3-Point Control Scheme for a Fault Tolerant Duplex Coil BLDC Motor Based Launch Vehicle Electromechanical Actuation System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Fault tolerance in aerospace and launch vehicle applications often entails introduction of additional identical signal or power chains to take over in case of a failure. A unique solution to failure mitigation in launch vehicle actuation system is the usage of a multi-coil motor. Such a motor consists of multiple independent stator coils driven by independent power drives. Under conditions of open coil failure, remaining coils should be able to meet the actuation demands. But a coil-short failure can degrade the performance of actuation as it will induce a breaking effect. Thus, it is pertinent that the controller be able to not only detect and distinguish between coil failures, but should initiate corrective actions to ensure performance. In this work the system under consideration is modelled under nominal and failure conditions. The suitability of an adaptive scheme in compensating the performance degradation is also studied. Simulation results validate the suitability of the adaptive scheme but also bring out certain shortcomings such as poor transient response at the time of failure and associated computational complexities. A 3-point control scheme to overcome these shortcomings while ensuring satisfactory performance of the actuation system under coil failure scenarios is proposed and validated. Simulation results corroborate the superior performance of the scheme.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation to analyze the effect of ambient temperature on impedance spectra of LIB for optimum BESS application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Commercially feasible battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are indispensable to deal with RE intermittency and increasing demand for frequency regulation. In the present scenario, it is crucial to intensify accurate and fast battery performance models for analyzing behavior under different operating conditions. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy has been widely used to realize the physics and chemistry of battery systems. Determination of optimum battery operating conditions pertaining to grid applications is still a concern. Integration of various parameters such as ambient temperature, battery parameters, and the corresponding changing available capacity of battery system in the model can lead to optimal operation of BESS. The impact of temperature and state of charge on the electrochemical impedance spectrum is investigated in the current study. This research article examines the influence of ambient temperature (varying from <tex>$15^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex>$35^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, with a progressive increase of <tex>$5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>) on the performance of Lithium-ion battery that utilizes electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for charged and discharged state of Lithium-ion battery. In addition, the relative change in the electrochemical impedance spectra for charged and discharged state of Lithiumion battery is presented. The analysis can be applied for the optimal operation of BESS. Qualitatively, the research highlights that the operation of BESS at a slightly higher temperature can realize higher capacity from the battery.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Parallel Prefix Adders Based on Carry Propagation and Sum Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Binary adders are an indispensable part of computing systems. There are different types of adders, they differ in terms of their structure and logic used. All these adders have been designed to achieve faster computation as possible. Parallel prefix adders (PPA) are one of the most efficient adders. In this work, PPAs such us Ladner-Fischer, Kogge-Stone, Brent-Kung, Knowles and Roy-auto synthesis adders were studied and compared in terms of delay, area and power. The adders now existing are using carry propagation (CP) as its fundamental concept to perform addition. Carry is a major problem in most of the adders because of its complexity and cost in the design of fast adders. The feasibility of performing addition without using carry i.e. by sum propagation (SP) concept is also analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Vienna Rectifier considering System Parasitic for off-Board EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The need for higher power ratings and efficient AC-DC conversion led to opting of Vienna Rectifier for off-board electric vehicle (EV) charging applications. In this paper, a complete analysis of three phase Vienna Rectifier considering the effect of parasitic in the system for off-board EV charging application is discussed. To improve the dynamic response a modified dual loop control using d-axis and q-axis current controller including the effect of system parasitic in control loops is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compared with different control algorithms viz., dual loop control using hysteresis current controller and dual loop control using d-axis and q-axis current controller with SVPWM. A comparative performance analysis is discussed in terms of dynamic response during system disturbances like load variation, reference DC bus voltage variation and grid side variations. A 50 kW Vienna Rectifier operating at a switching frequency of 200 kHz is used for performance evaluation of all three control algorithms and is validated using MATLAB-Simulink.

articleTitle: Load Margin Assessment of Power Systems Using Chaotic Crow Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The load margin is an important index to evaluate the operating complexity of power systems. This index commonly uses static models of power systems and determines the load margin related to the voltage stability threshold. However, load growth also causes the emergence of oscillation modes with low damping ratios that can cause small-signal instability of power systems. This work proposes a method to determine the load margin considering the operating restrictions of voltage stability and small-signal stability studies. This proposed method is based on an optimization model and it is solved by a metaheuristic called Crow Search Algorithm with the theory of Chaotic functions. Case studies are presented and evaluated in the IEEE 39-bus system.

articleTitle: Development of a Multipurpose Solar Powered Insect Pests Trap: KRISHI VIKAS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Pest management is one of the major expenditures that can drill a hole in a farmer's pocket. Pesticides have the potential to harm human health while also reducing soil fertility. In addition to killing insects, pesticides can be toxic to a host of other organisms, including birds, fish, and non-target plants. Though there are several models and designs available, it is a solar-powered system that is independent of conventional forms of energy. It is the best project due to its multipurpose use, eco-friendliness, cost-effectiveness, energy-efficient nature, and ease of handling. It helps to catch all the high-risk sucking pests like whiteflies, aphids, capsids, shore flies, leaf miners, cabbage root flies, thrips, etc., thereby reducing the adult population and subsequent progenies in the fields. The residues of these trapped flies can be turned into manure, which reduces waste. This feature will protect the farmers from the attacks of predators like snakes, etc. It acts as a street light while detecting human interference during the night. So it is an energy-efficient system. The system has a mobile charging facility and provides 5 V DC output. It also has a facility for the owners to keep the necessary things in the locker of the system while working. The Krishi Vikas were developed as an effective way of controlling insects in agricultural fields. It is both environmentally friendly and cost-effective for farmers. The system is fully automatic and powered by solar, so it can be used in rural village areas where there is no electricity. The whole system is modeled in Proteus.

articleTitle: Comparison of Sine-wave inverter topologies: Infinite-Level inverter and Differential inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The classic bridge inverter is outclassed by pulse width modulated voltage source inverters (PWMVSI), yet PWM inverters still face significant difficulties. Device restriction and significant switching loss cause major issues when power and voltage ratings increase. A variety of pulse width modulation techniques, including sinusoidal, third harmonic injection, and space vector PWM (SVPWM) use high frequency switching to provide high-quality output voltage with little ripple. In a multi-level inverter, increasing the number of active switches and passive components is necessary to raise the voltage levels. Compared to two-stage conversion, single-stage conversion has a more compact design, a better power density, and a cheaper cost. Two inverter topologies which produce sine wave output in single stage conversion are infinite level inverter and differential inverter. The infinite level inverter topology has a buck based active front end followed by an H-bridge. Differential inverters are single-stage, bidirectional DC-AC converters that can step up or down and invert the DC voltage. Three converters make up the majority of a differential inverter. Depending on the output needs, it can be a buck, boost, or buck-boost. The two converters are controlled so that the difference between their outputs produces an AC voltage at the desired frequency. In this paper infinite level inverter and buck converter based differential inverter is compared. Total switching device power, passive component requirement, and efficiency of each of these inverters were calculated. For purposes of comparison, both the inverters are given the same load, modulating signal and are operated from same DC voltage source to compare the losses and efficiency.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Analysis in Islanded Microgrid via Sliding Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this work, sliding mode control (SMC) technique is used for frequency control under load disturbance in microgrids (MGs). The MGs are well known for reliable, efficient, low cost and clean energy. They are often looked as a solution for future energy crisis, zero-emission energy sources, and a mean to optimally utilize the energy present in the nature. However, the stability of MGs has always been a matter of concern due to uncertain behavior of renewable energy sources like wind and solar. Any mismatch in the generation and load demand lead to frequency deviation from its scheduled value. Offset frequency lead to system instability and at worse may lead to large scale blackouts. In this work, a PI type sliding surface is used for better transient behavior. The control input ensures frequency stabilization under load disturbance. Frequency stabilization is also observed with the presence of typical nonlinearities like generation rate constraint (GRC) and governor deadband (GDB). The present work is compared to commonly used PI controller tuned using Ziegler Nichols method and ANN-GA algorithm. It is found that the frequency deviation using SMC has a better transient behavior compared to PI controller. The stability of SMC is verified theoretically using Lyapunov candidate function and validated using Simulink in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Power Decoupling Using Inductor In Triple Active Bridge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The rise in electricity demand has led to new solutions like distributed generation. It has always been difficult to integrate such distributed energy resources (DERs), and numerous approaches have been investigated to do so. Due to their various potential uses in EV charging systems, DC microgrids, and the integration of renewable energy sources, isolated DC-DC converters are growing in popularity. The Dual Active Bridge is a very promising method for integrating DERs (DAB). DAB is capable to integrate only two sources and if threes sources/loads are there then the system becomes bulkey and expensive. Hence, due to its various benefits, multiport isolated DC-DC converters are popular for integrating different energy resources. This paper discusses the Triple Active Bridge (TAB). The equivalent circuit is discussed along with its mathematics and Matlab simulation. The issue regarding the decoupling power flow is addressed, and a hardware-based decoupling solution is proposed.

articleTitle: Decentralized market model using Automated Market Maker for three-phase unbalanced distribution networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents a decentralized market model for future distribution networks where small-scale single-phase prosumers participate in the market along with three-phase prosumers. In the proposed model, the Energy Storage Units (ESU) make energy commitments for a trading period. The energy commitments along with the money are tokenized to form a liquidity pool. The prosumers located in different phases in the network can trade with this liquidity pool. The concept of Automated Market Maker (AMM) is employed for fast and iteration-free price discovery. The network constraints and distribution line power losses are considered in the model. The operation of the proposed market model is shown on IEEE 13 bus unbalanced distribution network.

articleTitle: A Simple, Linear Circuit for Measuring fF Range of Capacitances
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: There are numerous applications wherein capacitive sensing is performed such as, measurement of flow rates and environmental factors, dielectric testing, composition evaluation, proximity sensing, etc. Sometimes, the change brought on the capacitance of the sensor by the measurand may be in femto-Farad (fF) range. The circuitry required to measure changes this low can be very expensive and complex. So, a unique circuit was designed by the authors in one of their previous works that can detect such minute variations in capacitance without much complexity. This circuit does a differencing operation first, followed by a differential measurement to increase the sensitivity as well as to obtain linear outputs with respect to the capacitance measured. As a continuation, this paper presents the performance analysis of this circuit after some design modifications. The experimental results obtained were linear as per the theory of operation of this circuit and its sensitivity and repeatability were very good. However, a few parameters need improvement. But, as the results look promising on-the-whole, with suitable corrections, this circuit can be utilized for a wide variety of applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Binary Representational Image Approach for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This research proposes the use of a “binary representational image” for malware classification. The proposed solution used a deep learning approach to classify malware. There are several methods for analyzing and studying malware. The technique based on image processing and image classification is a novel approach to analyzing malware. Malware can be categorized according to its family types, making it easier to assess the damage the file could have or has already caused. A total of 35 categories of image families are used for classification. Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) are used in the proposed image-based classification system to detect malicious content. With CNN, the proposed method achieved an accuracy of 92.73

articleTitle: Bridge-less Dual Source Integrated Converter for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This study offers an isolated bridge-less integrated converter for electric vehicle (EV) applications that can charge the onboard battery and drive the traction motor under running conditions. A photovoltaic panel is integrated into the system as an additional range-extending source. While charging batteries from the grid, the proposed converter operates as an isolated bridge-less single ended primary inductance converter (SEPIC). In grid charging mode, the bridge-less architecture omits the traditional diode bridge rectifier on the input side, reducing the related conduction losses. During grid charging mode, the input current maintains a unity power factor with reduced total harmonic distortion without any wave shaping control circuitry and with reduced sensor requirements. PV charging mode is achieved when the grid is not connected to the system, and the converter operates as a standard SEPIC converter during charging. For propulsion, the integrated converter runs in boost mode. All of these operations are accomplished using the minimum number of components. Using MATLAB 2021, simulations are performed to evaluate the performance of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Coupling Enhancement of Hemispherical Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The proposed design describes a simple and new method to enhance the coupling of the hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna (HDRA) with waveguide feed. This is achieved by embedding a dielectric block of hard rubber inside the waveguide. The low permittivity material provides excellent coupling and impedance matching. Simulations have been done using Ansoft HFSS. The structure achieves a coupling of 98% at resonance frequency 9.02 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 5.2 % and a maximum gain of 6.35 dBi.

articleTitle: A Current Controlled Isolated Integrated AC/DC LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes the application of the boost integrated two-switch forward converter in current control mode for LED applications. Automatic power factor correction at the input is obtained with discontinuous mode (DCM) boost converter. The two-switch topology of forward converter reduces the switch voltage stresses compared to conventional forward topology. Also, transformer saturation is eliminated with reset diodes without the use of separate circuitry. The isolated integrated ac/dc LED driver circuit is simulated in matlab/Simulink software and obtained the results. The dimming capability of the driver is also observed.

articleTitle: A Combination of Optimal PWM Techniques for Control Across a Wide Modulation Range in Five Level Voltage-Source
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The genetic algorithm (GA) and Newton-Raphson (NR) methods are used in this study to present an effective selective harmonic elimination (SHE) approach for a cascaded five-level inverter with six switching angles (N=6) every quarter cycle. For induction motor drive systems, a mixed PWM technique based on the distribution ratios 5/1, 3/3, and 1/5 is recommended in order to accomplish wide modulation range management. By resolving a series of nonlinear transcendental equations, the optimal switching angles for the three different distribution ratios are calculated while retaining the desired fundamental voltage and successfully removing the low order non-triplen odd harmonics up to the <tex>$17^{th}$</tex> harmonic order <tex>$(THD_{17})$</tex>. Additionally, in order to find the best solution that produces the least total harmonic distortion up to the <tex>$49^{th}$</tex> harmonic order, numerous existing solutions for each value of the modulation indices are assessed and compared. The findings demonstrate that the five non-triplen low order harmonics i.e. the fifth, seventh, eleventh, thirteenth, and seventeenth are successfully removed from the inverter line voltage output, and that the least <tex>$THD_{49}$</tex> is obtained when utilizing the suggested method for a broad modulation range.

articleTitle: Tuning of PID Controller in Magnetic Levitation System Applying Honey Badger Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper is intended for control and stabilization of the Magnetic Levitation (Maglev) system wherein a magnetic ball is levitated in space under the influence of a magnetic field. The Maglev system, which is highly unstable in nature, is made to stabilize with use of a PID controller in feedback. The values of gains of the PID controller can be found after applying metaheuristic algorithms. In this study, the Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA) has been employed to determine the gains of the PID controller. HBA is a recently developed algorithm that offers a good balance of speed of convergence and exploration and exploitation. Various time domain parameters like Settling time, Peak time, Rise time, and Maximum Overshoot are computed and compared with differently tuned PID gain values using various algorithms. The results obtained after applying HBA are compared to those of the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to validate the efficacy of the applied algorithm.

articleTitle: Newspaper Article Summarization Using Combinational Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Text summarization produces a concise amount of data out of document which may represent the core information contained in the document. In this paper, a combinational approach has been used to generate summary from newspaper article that uses a number of features to rank sentences of the article. Graph based approach with minimal text sentiment analysis and the presence of category wise key phrases have been used. Sentences with the sentiment polarity of the overall document sentiment polarity can convey important information. Combination of multiple features can lead to the identification process of the significant sentences with which good summary can be formed. After the performance analysis of the approach, it has been observed that the technique can generate good summaries that are close to human written ones.

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of degradation parameters using dynamic mode decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The parameter estimation of the nonlinear system demands complex estimation algorithms. Recently data-driven modeling such as Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) and Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control (DMDc), has gained popularity in the field of parameter estimation and system identification of complex non-linear systems. In this paper, we have applied the DMDc technique for system identification and parameter estimation of the DC motor and DC-DC buck converter with and without knowledge of the input matrix. Further, this helps in condition monitoring and predictive maintenance of different passive components in the buck converter, such as capacitors and resistors. The results conclude that the DMD estimates those parameters within a tolerance limit of 2.2% with a minimum number of data required to capture the dynamics of the system.

articleTitle: Initial Results with Real-Time Testing of Smart-WAMS for Power Oscillation Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This article illustrates the laboratory based real-time testing of smart wide-area monitoring systems (smart-W AMS). The smart-WAMS approach has already been published by the authors of this paper and it has been proven very effective in wide-area monitoring of power oscillations. Smart-WAmsconsumes the phasor measurement unit (PMU) signal and gives the accurate real-time information about the various critical modes present in the system. The dominant low frequency modes can be tracked in real-time in terms of its frequency and amplitude deviation. The testing is done using real-time simulator, Opal-RT. The two power system networks are considered for testing. The first one is the offline IEEE 39 bus system which is simulated in real-time environment in Opal-RT and the second one is the online Nordic grid system. The procedure and the relevant details involved in the testing are explained and the obtained results are also discussed.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Radix-4 Adder and Accuracy-Configurable Radix-4 Adder
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper a comparative study of normal Radix-4 Adder (RD4A) and Accuracy-Configurable Radix-4 Adder (ACRA) is presented. The RD4A decreases the propagation delay and power consumption of traditional adders such as ripple carry adder (RCA) and carry-lookahead adder (CLA) by operating two bits simultaneously. To reduce the power consumption further and reconfiguring the computational accuracy an ACRA could be used. This accuracy-adjustable adder could be used for various error-tolerant applications. The simulation results obtained from Xilinx ISE 14.7 and comparison between the RD4A and ACRA is presented in this paper. In order to construct a multi-bit adder an RD4A and numerous ACRAs could be added to an ACRA based fully-configurable adder. To further improve the performance of above-mentioned adder an ACRA and PPA (parallel prefix adder) based hybrid adder could be used.

articleTitle: SOGI-PLL-based control scheme for PFC Boost Converter under Distorted Grid Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Nowadays in an electrical power system various DC-to-DC converters are widely used due to their variable range in output and efficient power conversion, but they draw current in form of pulses making the power factor of the system poor and Total Harmonic Distortion(THD) very high. For linear load, the correction of power factor can be done via passive load but with non-linear load, the distorted current line needs to be corrected with various control schemes. In this paper popular topology for Active Power Factor Correction(APFC) i.e boost converter has been studied in a power system under distorted main supply voltage, needing higher current compensation. A method for elimination of harmonic distortion from the input supply voltage is done with the means of SOGI-PLL, providing an inexpensive solution. This paper discusses all the steps for the straightforward control design of the PFC+PLL along with design criteria and calculations. The design and simulation of the boost converter with power factor correction in continuous conduction mode are modelled using MATLAB/SIMULINK software.

articleTitle: Solar PV fed Non-Isolated DC-DC Multiport Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Multiport converters (MPC) design is promising from the point of view of centralized control and compact packaging. The basic bidirectional switching cells present several possibilities for constructing a multiport converter. This paper discusses a technique which is termed as switched-boost action, it produces two controlled ports using time-multiplexing of switches. This technique permits regulation and control of all the outputs while utilising comparatively fewer switches. An alternative to traditional DC-DC topology, multiple-output converters with a single input source are now being researched in order to increase power density in small powered multiload appliances. With the help of a switched boost MPC, a solar panel with battery storage system and household loads are connected. The battery is connected to the 12 V bus. The converter's functionality is tested with solar PV, which feeds a 12 V battery and a 36 V load bus. The converter automatically switches to a mode in which the 12 V battery powers the loads on the 36 V bus when solar power is absent.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Self-Adjust Optimal Air Conditioning Temperature using Differential Air Velocity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Temperature prediction in cooling systems is a significant theme within the application domain of IoT and Machine Learning. It is tough to vary the temperature during sleeping hours, meeting times, and for the most part, wherever an arbitrarily large number of people occupy a room. There are several parameters that play a pivotal role in deciding the accuracy of temperature predictions made by automatic systems, which include the quality and quantity of the data used to train the machine learning model, the complexity of the model, and the variability of the environment in which the air conditioner is used. Automatic temperature prediction also improves comfort levels for building occupants, as the air conditioner is set to maintain the predicted comfortable temperature without requiring manual adjustments. The proposed Intelligent Air Conditioning system in the paper can predict the desired temperature of the user and self-adjust the predicted temperature of the room automatically using IoT and Machine Learning techniques. The algorithm deployed in the system inputs various physical parameters such as humidity, AQI, altitude, atmospheric pressure, number of occupants, room dimensions, ambient light, light intensity, and air velocity to ensure accurate temperature predictions. If the predicted temperature does not match the comfort temperature recommended by ASHRAE, the system will cool/condition the room with a temperature within the range of comfort temperature recommended by ASHRAE and close to the predicted temperature. The ceiling fan unit is employed to compensate for the temperature difference without decreasing the room temperature using differential air velocity. This promising technology will satisfy the complete level of automation through Image processing, Machine Learning, and IoT.

articleTitle: Complementary Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Variable Speed Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The reduction in transient loads on the drive train influences the life span of the wind turbine when designing the controller for power extraction. In wind turbines, compromises between the efficiency of power extraction and the load level on the drive train have become key issues. Conventional control techniques enhanced energy extraction at the cost of a higher transient load on the drive train. Therefore, this work proposes the complementary terminal sliding mode controller for energy extraction whilst reducing the drive train load. A 600 kW FAST simulator is utilised to validate the performance of the proposed and conventional controllers. Finally, a detailed investigation has been conducted based on energy extraction and mitigation of transient loads under various turbulence models and mean wind speeds.

articleTitle: A Simulative Study on Operational Transconductance Amplifiers in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: An operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) is a voltage controlled current source. In analog circuits and systems that earlier uses operational amplifiers to implement operational transconductance. The modern world is focused on the advancement of VLSI technology, and everything is connected to transistor size and a circuit's reducing power supply. Operational transconductance amplifiers are frequently employed in analog circuits, such as filtering, converters, and instrument amplifiers. The comparative study of OTAs is presented in this paper. Both SI-OTA and MI-OTA are implemented using <tex>$0.18-\mu m$</tex> CMOS technology from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). Simulation results illustrate that the MIOTAs are having better performance in terms of power and delay.

articleTitle: A Survey of Bi-directional DC-DC Converters for Transportation Electrification and Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Concern for the environment and dwindling fossil fuel resources has increased the attention towards sustainable alternatives by governments, industries, and consumers. This has resulted in an increased emphasis on transportation electrification and renewable energy systems. Bi-directional DC-DC converters find their applications in various fields of transportation electrification like electric vehicles, more-electric aircraft, and all-electric ships. It also finds extensive use in microgrids for interfacing renewable energy storage systems to the supply bus and load. This paper presents a review of various bidirectional DC-DC converter topologies that can be used in these applications. Among the converters reviewed, the dual active bridge converter is simulated in MATLAB and the results are obtained.

articleTitle: A study on the impact of hall sensor toggling at magnetic crossover points in a fault tolerant quadruplux BLDC motor for aerospace applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The paper presents a study on the behavior of a fault tolerant quadruplex winding BLDC motor at points of magnetic crossover. The AC component introduced in the coil current due to the hall sensor output alternating between two adjacent patterns is studied in the paper. The torque ripple due to the induced AC component of current is analyzed. The effect of frequency of variation in the rotor position when commanded to stay exactly at the point of magnetic crossover and its effect on the coil current is brought out through simulations. The drawbacks associated with sensing the current in the battery return line and using it for closing the current loop, at the magnetic change over points, are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Recursive Least Squares based Dynamic Model Predictive Control for Grid-Tied Active Front End Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The classical current control techniques for grid connected LCL type active front-end converters (AFEs) are usually interacts with the phase locked loop (PLL) nonlinearities and grid impedance, thus deteriorates the stability of the converter which leads to system instability. In order to avoid the stability issues, this manuscript provides a simpler and much better recursive least square based dynamic model predictive current control technique to approximate the attributes of physical model to their true value. In this control structure the predicted variables are evaluated using the cost function at each sample interval and the most efficient switching state with the lowest cost function value is chosen. According to the estimated switching states, the gate pulses are generated for the AFEs switches. The performance of the proposed control structure is tested using simulation platform under a widespread range of variations in grid impendence and system's nonlinearities. Under these conditions, the suggested method which considers the system's nonlinearities provides outstanding resilience in high and medium frequency grid dynamics. Furthermore, the simulations results have been varied through hardware platform using Typhoon HIL to show the advantages of proposed control over classical controls.

articleTitle: A Review on Various in-pipe Inspection Methods for a Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this contemporary world, one of the major mode of transportation for hydrocarbon fluids are pipelines. The pipes should be designed and constructed in order to stay healthy and safe for various environmental conditions and different loading conditions. Pipeline defects and leakage due to failures may cause danger to environment, humans and leads to heavy financial losses. So periodic inspection is a very important procedure and there are many methods available for the leakage detection and localization. These methods are discussed and compare in this paper.

articleTitle: Design and Power Flow Control in Standalone PV System with Reduced Battery Current Ripple
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: To improve solar photovoltaic (PV) panel efficiency, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm is needed, which could help to extract the optimal power from solar PV systems. The adaptive backstepping controlling approach is presented in this paper for tracking maximum power points in PV systems. The controller is based on the Lyapunov stability theory and connects the selection of an appropriate Lyapunov function with the design of feedback control action. The reference voltages which are generated for the controller are generated through the maximum power voltage (MPV) searching algorithm. The battery energy storage system (BESS) is linked to a bidirectional converter, which governs both the DC bus voltage and the power flow from the BESS. The operation of the DC microgrid is addressed under varying irradiance changes. Further, the impact of ripple current on the battery heating and its performance are discussed. MATLAB/Simulink software is used to simulate and validate the effectiveness of a BESS-enabled isolated solar PV-based system.

articleTitle: A Novel Partial Shading Detection and Maximum Power Harvesting Algorithm for Reconfigurable PV Array
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Partial Shading is a vital cause for loss of generation capability of a PV array. If PS is not adequately resolved, as an outcome, the PV string will experience a mismatching current that causes hot spots, module failure, and other unfavourable effects. Abundant techniques have been considered to alleviate these challenges. In this paper, a hybridised method, optimized with Power Mismatch Optimization Algorithm and Partial Shading Detection is proposed to tackle the aforementioned challenges. The aim of the proposed work is to separate uniform shading conditions from Partial Shading Conditions (PSCs) and generate optimal energy utilising with set row and column placements of modules under shading conditions. Short bottom-wide shading situations have been used to analyse and evaluate under Total-Cross-Tied PV array configuration. Furthermore, it prevents PSCs from having an excessive global peak search. The performance of the proposed method includes an increase in power output, a reduction in multiple peaks and a mismatch current. Moreover, this article has also proposed a solution for power and current variance that prevents the unbalancing of the strings. The simulation outcomes can efficiently differentiate PS events and improve a power gain of 29.83%, and a fill factor of 76.02%.

articleTitle: Automated Irrigation System for Efficient and Portable Farming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The practise of farming has endured significant transformation as technology advances every day. The constraints of area and nonlinear nature of climatic conditions, polyhouse kind of concepts are increasing, which is helpful in production of flowers, vegetables and fruits. The proposed work discusses such an automated irrigation system that highlights the optimum solution for the efficient use of water and electricity for agricultural purposes. Field survey and literature shows that the existing systems are available with two solutions, one is timer-based and another one is moisture-based automization. Moreover, the timer-based system has demerits like being semi-automated i.e., timer needs to be changed manually according to climate. Similarly, in moisture-based systems, reliability is the issue. Therefore, the main objectives of the proposed work are to overcome the demerits of the present systems by integrating both the systems, to develop a fully automated irrigation system, to manage the use of water, electricity, and to add a remote controlling system. The report includes algorithm for the integration of moisture and timer-based system which provides the optimum efficiency on the water use and the use of solenoidal valve.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Fault-Tolerant Interleaved Buck Converter for Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: DC-DC converters are one of the most important and challenging subsystems in charging systems. The reliability of the system has always been an issue because of the failures of the semiconductor switches. The paper presents the design of a 1kW fault-tolerant interleaved buck converter for battery charging applications. It also proposes an algorithm for detection of fault in any of the switches and uses a redundant leg-based topology so that the converter functions like the prior fault condition. The algorithm makes use of the digitally implemented circuit and hence does-not affect the cost of the system much. A modified PI control which works along with fault detection and control scheme is implemented to charge the battery in constant current mode which do not let current and voltage ripples increase after the fault. Also, it distributes the current equally to avoid stress over a particular branch. The modified control alters the faulty phase with the redundant phase after the occurrence of the fault with the help of fault detection system. The fault-tolerant capability ensures the continuous operation of the converter even after a fault and made it suitable for electric vehicle battery charging applications.

articleTitle: Control of Hybrid PV System with Battery Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: A control scheme for a hybrid solar inverter is proposed which can operate the inverter in both ‘on grid’ and ‘off grid’ modes and have a seamless transfer between the two methods. The input for this inverter is obtained from multiple strings of PV arrays. An individual maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for each string is implemented to optimize the power extraction from the PV module. A battery bank controlled by a charge-discharge regulator is interfaced with the DC bus of the inverter. In grid-connected mode, this battery bank can be charged from the grid as well as from the PV panel depending on user preference. In off-grid mode, this battery compensates for the mismatch between the generation from the PV panel and the load. The proposed control scheme for the hybrid solar inverter is validated through extensive simulation studies.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimizer Applied to the Wide-Area Damping Controller Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Data from PMUs from remote locations proved to be useful for improving the observability of power systems and many applications have been proposed. The development of the Wide-Area Damping Controller (WADC) that uses data from PMUs is effective in damping control of inter-area oscillation modes of power systems. However, the design of WADC robust to communication failures is still a challenge. This article proposes an optimization model for the design of WADC robust to communication failures, the metaheuristic Grey Wolf Optimizer is used to solve the optimization problem and an initialization procedure for the variables of the optimization problem is proposed. Case studies are presented and discussed for the IEEE 68 bus system.

articleTitle: In-house developed 32-bit Digital Signal Processor for Strategic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Avionics systems rely on digital signal processing algorithms for various applications like Navigation, Guidance and Control, Image and Data Processing etc. Digital Signal Processors (DSPs) are typically used to implement these algorithms, which require intense iterative computations to be performed on large data sets. DSPs generally provide special addressing modes, dedicated hardware blocks and enhanced parallelism to meet the stringent timing requirements of these computations. Commercial DSPs are available in various ranges of capability and speed, however, their use in strategic applications is governed by their availability and reliability criteria. Usage of commercial DSPs is made difficult due to long lead times, obsolescence, import restrictions and cost. In this work, we present the architecture and design of a scalable 32-bit Floating point DSP, with an in-house developed architecture, instruction set, assembly language and software toolset. The DSP provides high performance in terms of fast execution, low overhead and interrupt latency, making it suitable for time critical DSP applications. The DSP also implements special instructions, called algorithmic instructions, which provide hardware acceleration for selected computation intensive operations. The performance of the DSP in executing commonly used signal processing algorithms compares well with commercial DSPs currently used in avionics systems. The design is currently implemented as a core in Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), making use of the internal memory blocks of the FPGA to hold program and data. Different versions of the DSP have been flown in various Satellite and Launch Vehicle avionics systems.

articleTitle: Comparison of Faster RCNN and YOLO V3 for Video Anomaly Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Video Anomaly Localization techniques are interesting and emerging tasks in computer vision that is used to locate the position of an anomalous object with bounding boxes. Convolutional neural network-based object localization methods have been developed which detect and classify objects with high precision and accuracy. Many algorithms have been developed for object detection and localization with excellent outcomes. These algorithms are fast RCNN, faster RCNN, and YOLO. In this paper, a comprehensive analysis of faster RCNN and YOLO V3 algorithms for anomaly localization is performed based on the parameters FPS, mAP, Precision, Recall and F1 Score.

articleTitle: A Boost PFC fed LLC Resonant Converter For Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper describes a half-bridge LLC resonant converter followed by a power factor corrected (PFC) boost converter in an electric car battery. The suggested charger employs a boost converter as the front-end dc-dc converter, which operates in continuous conduction mode (CCM) of the input inductor to provide harmonic-free AC mains current. As the second stage, a Half-Bridge LLC resonant converter is used to accelerate battery charging. An active power factor controller (APFC) manages the DC-link voltage while also maintaining sinusoidal input current. Pulse frequency modulation (PFM) is used after the PI-controller to adjust the battery's output. On the MATLAB/Simulink platform, the proposed charger's steady-state and dynamic performance are evaluated for a range of supply voltage and load conditions.

articleTitle: Architectural Design of Malware Infected File Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: I. Abstract Currently, with the ongoing development of 5G and the IoT Cyberspace has grown to be a significant part of social and economic development thanks to the technology of social and economic development, as well as a fundamental domain of national security. Therefore, the detection of Malware and its variations are extremely important in cyberspace. Malware is a harmful software that is designed to damage and destroy computers and computer systems. Malware is constantly generating, updating, and manipulating which makes the detection more challenging. Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware, Adware, etc. are the common types of malware attacks. Signature based, Behavioral based and Heuristic ones are the three main methods used for malware detection. This paper discusses the architectural design for malware prediction in executable files of various applications and visualization techniques used to achieve better results by creating RGB images of these executable files and try to convert the malware prediction method into an image classification problem. InceptionV3 and the SVM model are used for feature extraction and prediction. Leopard mobile dataset and Malimg dataset are used here.

articleTitle: A Non-Isolated Three Port DC/DC Converter to Integrate Solar PV and Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Nowadays renewable energy sources are increasingly used by concerning environmental awareness. By integrating an energy storage system overcomes the intermittent nature of these renewable energy sources. So, a non-isolated three-port DC-DC converter is developed for integrating renewable energy sources and energy storage systems. To combine a PV battery DC power system, the presented converter has two unidirectional photovoltaic (PV), load ports and one bidirectional battery port. The main features of this converter are high efficiency, high integration capability, and a reduced number of components. The theoretical analysis was conducted to study all working modes, and a small-signal model of this converter was developed utilizing the state-space method. Extensive simulation has been carried out to verify the finding in all operating modes.

articleTitle: Privacy Prevention Techniques in Cyber Physical System for Pharmaceutical Care Services
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: By implementing Cyber Physical Systems, pharmaceutical businesses may significantly improve healthcare, utility, safety, and environmental health (CPS). But these service enhancements and cost-cutting initiatives will make people more vulnerable and at risk. Intruders employ passive attacks to obtain access to CPSs' private information. Some privacy preservation methods have previously been made available in order to increase the security of the data held by PCPS. However, these techniques also need to be altered due to changes in the PCPS's architecture. In this study, privacy prevention techniques in CPS for health care services including prescription medicines have been evaluated. Opportunities for future research are also acknowledged, along with a number of difficulties.

articleTitle: A Review on FPGA Implementation of Lightweight Cryptography for Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become increasingly popular in recent years due to their ability to remotely monitor and gather data in a variety of applications. The frequent exchange of confidential data over the network makes WSNs vulnerable to various attacks that can threaten their security. To mitigate these attacks security services such as confidentiality, authentication, and integrity is required. The interacting devices in the network can be authenticated and the transmitted data can be protected using encryption methods. As WSNs are resource-limited, it is a challenge to develop and implement an encryption algorithm that is secure and resource-efficient. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) initiated the lightweight cryptography (LWC) project to standardize lightweight cryptography algorithms, useful for constrained environments where current standards are not acceptable. Lightweight cryptographic algorithms are designed to provide adequate security and performance while not being computationally very expensive. The combination of cryptographic algorithms with hardware can significantly increase the security level, efficiency, and lifetime of the sensor node. This paper presents a comparative study of the NIST LWC finalists, evaluating the top variants based on design and FPGA benchmarking metrics such as block size, performance parameters, and security. All of the ciphers were implemented and tested on Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA. Finally, the paper discusses some optimization measures and future directions for the use of lightweight cryptographic coprocessors in WSNs.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing and IoT Integration: Issues, Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The demand for connection in our daily lives has led to the adoption of more devices than ever before that are connected to the Internet and one another. As a result, the storage, exchange, and processing of data in modern times are significantly influenced by integrating technologies. With the help of the Internet of Things (IoT), many devices can connect to the web and generate a ton of data. In contrast, cloud computing serves as a paradigm for providing universal, useful, on-demand network access to a shared pool of computing resources with the least amount of administrative burden. IoT benefits greatly from cloud computing since it offers essential services. IoT development is heavily reliant on the availability of cloud services like computational power and storage. The cloud-based IoT paradigm opens up new possibilities while efficiently utilizing infrastructure, apps, and data. This study draws attention to the issues and practical challenges associated with integrating these two technologies. The study also makes an effort to describe the benefits of integration and discusses future applications for cloud IoT.

articleTitle: Beyond 5G Communication Networks Enabling Massive IOT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The future of humanity is dependent upon the IOT(Internet of things) and 5G network, which means most of the machine and mobile phones and devices are operating through the IOT(Internet of things) and to transfer the data from one port to another port through the 5G network and it is seen that it play an very crucial role in this area. To use this IOT(Internet of things) have to create an advanced intelligent environment into the world which is running through the human command, voice like example amazon ALEXA device, most of AC system which operated with the phone and audio. When a large number of the device is operated with some device then some large number interaction between the heterogonous device and increase the demand like strong connection, exceptionally high data throughput, low latency, creating applications that play critical roles in IOT(Internet of things), as a result of this need 5G technology is an important facilitator for IOT(Internet of things) technology. this work gives all the theoretical information about the IOT(Internet of things) and 5G technology, also give the detail that how the technology is changing day by day due to this technology and it is going to be large scale in future for every single child and old person, so this work helps all gathering information about Latest technologies and work in this field.

articleTitle: An Asynchronous Exciter fed Brushless Wound Field Synchronous Motor Drive for Electrified Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept using a brushless wound field synchronous motor as a viable solution for Electrified Vehicle (EV) traction motor. It initially presents a comparative discussion between the main EV traction machines used presently and subsequently presents the system configuration of a proposed asynchronous exciter fed brushless wound field synchronous machine. For the proposed topology, a wound rotor induction machine (WRIM) is used along with a rotating diode bridge rectifier to control the field excitation of the wound field synchronous machine (WFSM), thus eliminating the need of the slipring-brush assembly. For the design of the overall proposed machine, the Toyota Prius 2004 traction interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) has been considered as the baseline and the basic stator frame size, airgap length and also the shaft diameter of the WFSM has been considered to be the same as that of Toyota Prius 2004 IPMSM. The rotor for the proposed wound field synchronous motor is designed and presented along with its FEM based simulation results. This is followed by the complete design and Finite Element Method (FEM) based simulation of the exciter induction machine. Indirect rotor flux-oriented vector control is applied on the exciting induction machine to control the excitation of the synchronous motor generating a minimal motoring torque for the exciter machine. Vector control is applied on the wound field synchronous motor component to satisfy the required tractive torque keeping the d-axis component of its armature reaction at zero.
